name: Refugee Status (Condición de Refugiado)

qualifying_event.description: A person outside their country of origin with a well-founded fear of persecution may apply for refugee status with Peru's Special Commission for Refugees (CEPR), under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (RREE). Regular/legal entry into Peru is not required to apply.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Application form; identity documents (or a sworn declaration if undocumented); for applicants 15+, a sworn statement on criminal/police record.

requirements.blocker_text: Applicant must show a well-founded fear of persecution, assessed by the Comisión Especial para los Refugiados (CEPR).
Application filed in person, with handwritten signature, at a CEPR Protection Space in Lima or a deconcentrated regional office.
requirements.fix_path: File a refugee status application with the CEPR.

evidence_required.document: Passport, national ID, or birth certificate (or loss/theft report plus sworn declaration if undocumented)

outcome.duration_length: not confirmed in this pass; provisional 'Carne de solicitante' historically valid 60 days, renewable, while the claim is pending

sources.title: Superintendencia Nacional de Migraciones (MIGRACIONES) -- Reglamento del Decreto Legislativo N.1350, Article 29.2.n: refugee/political asylum status recognized under Peru's international treaty commitments, processed by RREE/CEPR, 1-year duration

UNHCR Help Peru -- refugee status application process: CEPR (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) runs determination directly, no regular entry required, virtual work authorization after registration, provisional Carne de solicitante, confidentiality guarantee

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Peru). STATUS: DRAFT -- the category's existence and its 1-year duration are tier-1 (direct from the MIGRACIONES regulation, Art. 29.2.n), but the actual application process, document list, and interim rights during the pending period come from UNHCR (tier-2), not an independently fetched RREE/CEPR government page (portal.rree.gob.pe's dedicated refugee pages were not successfully fetched in this pass). No specific processing timeline was found -- disclosed as unconfirmed rather than guessed. Peru hosts one of the world's largest populations of displaced Venezuelans; most of that population holds ordinary temporary-stay or work permits (via the now-lapsed PTP/CPP regularization programs) rather than formal refugee status -- this file models the FORMAL 1951-Convention refugee determination route specifically, not the broader ad hoc regularization schemes, which are not modeled here since they are not an ongoing, generally-available route.
